summary: Kaniksu National Forest L-4 tower near Clark Fork, Idaho, built around 1934 and destroyed in 1961; no source describes the site today.

facts.status_note: Destroyed in 1961; no source describes what remains

events.note: Tower with L-4 cab; firelookout.com gives 1934, Idaho Fire Lookouts gives 1934 L-4 Tower, and Forest Lookouts Idaho gives c.1934
Item quoted by Forest Lookouts Idaho links Floyd Hamilton to the lookout in September 1937; his job is not stated
All three sources date the destruction to 1961

evidence.supports: built 1934 as an L-4 tower; destroyed 1961
about three miles north-northwest of Clark Fork
site code 56N-2E-21 on the Forest Lookouts Idaho page
1937 item attributed to the Northern Idaho News
Floyd Hamilton visiting home from the Howe Mountain lookout
evidence.quote: Floyd Hamilton, from Howe mountain lookout is visiting at home this week.

notes_for_editor: Build and destruction dates agree across all three pages, but the Forest Lookouts Idaho page credits its dates to Kresek and the other two pages do not name a source, so they may not be independent. Only one item, the 1937 Northern Idaho News mention, names a person connected to the lookout, and it is quoted second-hand. No source describes the site today. A search result suggested a possible mix-up with a 1934 L-4 tower at Diamond Peak (Kaniksu NF, Washington); that was not checked. The Idaho Fire Lookouts page shows a photo credit to the Bonner County Historical Society (Chuck Peterson collection) but no image URL was captured, so no photo is added. Brief record: no correction needed.
